sources.subject: QSA: exact sampled filter select and pooled BF16 mirror (opt-in)
sources.commit_message:
QSA: exact sampled filter select and pooled BF16 mirror (opt-in)

Two developer switches, both default off, both byte-exact by contract:

HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_FILTER_SELECT (eager gfx11+ score/select calls with
more than 4096 pooled blocks, budget <= 512): the single-workgroup
select-from-scores pass is replaced by three kernels in the new
kernels/src/qsa_filter_select.hip: a deterministic 2048-sample threshold
(exact j-th largest sample key, target 1024 survivors), tiled candidate
compaction (4096 blocks per workgroup, wave-ballot slot reservation,
capacity 4096) and an exact finish that ranks the certified candidate set
(chosen <= count <= cap) by the incumbent 64-bit key (score bits desc,
block asc). Underfilled or overflowing rows repair in-kernel with an exact
64-bit radix select over the whole row; output never depends on atomic
order. Selected tokens, causal tails, -1 padding and the final-row mirror
follow the incumbent contract byte for byte. Lab entries
(qsa_filter_select_from_scores_lab, qsa_incumbent_select_from_scores_lab,
indexed_attention_select_batch_filter_arm) expose per-row threshold /
count / repair stats.

HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_POOLED_BF16 (exact gfx1151, F32 QSA state): each QSA
layer keeps a derived BF16 mirror of its pooled index keys (the high
halves of the BF16-rounded F32 keys, lossless), synced past a block
watermark after pooling, never snapshotted, clamped/invalidated at every
existing F16-arena lifecycle site and charged in admission/state
accounting. Mirror-covered select calls run the PM BF16 rows16 score
instead of the F32 one (half the key bytes); the F32 arena stays
authoritative. IndexedAttentionSelectBatch gains `pooled_bf16`.

Evidence: crates/rdna-compute/tests/qsa_filter_select.rs on gfx1201
(R9700): 3 tests pass, 6048 from-scores and 432 full-route cases equal
to the hipcc incumbent incl. forced underfill/overflow repair. Mirror:
qwen4_qsa_arena_check four arms (off/on/pooled/pooled+arena) with
identical canonical selection/attention/state/logit hashes through
prefill, rollback, branch and restore; 14 mirror-consistency checks over
990,372 blocks; Halo Flash-Next nat-32K AR 128-token ids identical
on vs off.

sources.subject: QSA filter select: admit only past the measured select crossover
sources.commit_message:
QSA filter select: admit only past the measured select crossover

The filter trio beats the hipcc select-from-scores from 8192 blocks but
the gfx1151 PM select only further out. Halo per-call medians (5 warm,
50 timed): 1-16 rows PM 18.6 / 50.7 us vs filter 37 / 39 us at 8192 /
32768 blocks; 256 rows PM 0.26 / 1.15 ms vs filter 0.35 / 0.80 ms at
32768 / 65536 blocks. Calls running the PM select now take the filter
above 24576 blocks (<= 16 rows) or 49152 blocks (more rows); the hipcc
select keeps the 4096-block admission. Selection bytes are unchanged on
every route.

QSA: filter select and pooled BF16 mirror on by default on gfx1151

Both exact levers from fbea29a85/35cedf64d become the gfx1151 default:
HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_POOLED_BF16 defaults on (admission unchanged: exact
gfx1151, F32 QSA state, PM BF16 score present) and
HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_FILTER_SELECT defaults on for exact gfx1151 (unset
elsewhere keeps it off; =1 forces any gfx11+); =0 stays the kill switch
for both. Evidence (Halo, Flash-Next GPTQ3): greedy ids identical on the
8-prompt lane AR cell and on natural-text 8K/32K/128K/256K in every rep;
pooled-mirror arena hashes identical; decode ITL at 32K/128K/256K lower
in both candidate reps than in both base reps (8K tie): 30.73/31.21/33.11
-> 29.88/30.48/31.43 ms. Docs: env-vars rows, CONFIG QSA paragraph,
CHANGELOG entry and measured table.

sources.subject: perf(qwen4/gfx1151): opt-in split-K QSA decode attention (HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_DECODE_SPLITK, default off)
sources.commit_message:
perf(qwen4/gfx1151): opt-in split-K QSA decode attention (HIPFIRE_QWEN4_QSA_DECODE_SPLITK, default off)

- New kernels/src/qsa_decode_splitk.hip: qsa_decode_splitk_partial_f32 splits each
  row's selected list into 32 contiguous slices; one workgroup per (KV head, slice)
  scores all 12 query heads of its KV group from a single K/V read and writes
  (max, sum, acc[256]) partials; qsa_decode_splitk_combine_f32 folds the partials
  in ascending slice order and applies the output gate.
- Routed only inside indexed_attention_attention_batch_arena for eager gfx1151 F32
  head_dim-256 launches of 1..8 rows (AR decode and MTP verify); a row's output is
  bitwise independent of the launch row count. Partials reuse the per-launch QSA
  scratch. Every other launch keeps the incumbent route.
- fp32 reorder: KLD-gated, not bit-exact. GPU tests (tests/qsa_decode_splitk.rs):
  tolerance vs the incumbent, row invariance 1..8, all-invalid rows.

sources.subject: qwen4: a retired native-MTP turn catches its head up and commits live
sources.commit_message:
qwen4: a retired native-MTP turn catches its head up and commits live

Once the AR floor retires a request, its AR tokens advance the target
alone and the MTP head used to stay at the retirement point. The turn
then ended with the head behind the target, session_commit_live dropped
the live state (live continuation needs head == target), and the next
turn of the conversation restored the newest chunk snapshot and
re-prefilled everything above it (Strix Halo, 32K agent chain: 9,613 rows,
4.8 s, after a max_tokens stop where 55 rows were new).

A retired AR token now copies its target wide hidden into the next spec
hidden row and owes the head that row (HeadLag). catch_up_head appends
the owed rows teacher-forced (token p, target hidden p), exactly as an
n-gram takeover appends its kept rows: one batched decode fill where it
runs, else one Append per row. It runs when the owed rows fill one batched
fill (1024) and before every teacher-forced advance, so the terminal
pending-seed flush leaves head and target together and the turn commits
live. Resets, prefills and new requests drop the record.

Tests: HeadLag CPU tests; session_cache_hw
retired_turn_commits_live_on_flash_next (--features lab, ignored HW).

sources.message:
qwen4: replay tool-call turns as the emitted body, not a template re-render

A Flash-Next follow-up turn whose history held an assistant tool call
rendered that turn through the chat template: the jinja history splice
treated a cached content-only turn on a message with tool_calls as
structural doubt and fell back to a plain template render of the whole
history. That render is a strict extension of the committed conversation
only while the model's output is exactly the template's canonical
tokenization; a different BPE split of the emitted text, or spacing the
template rewrites around <tool_call> (trimmed content, its own \n\n before
the block), breaks the live continuation and re-prefills the whole
conversation. On the real Flash-Next tokenizer and template a non-canonical
split diverges at token 354 (thinking off) / 408 (thinking on) of a 2-tool
conversation; with canonical model output (observed on Strix Halo) the
re-render already matched.

Every stored Qwen turn already holds the producer's whole generated body
(reasoning, prose and the <tool_call> blocks). build_cached_history_jinja_with
takes a ToolTurnSplice: Envelopes keeps today's behaviour (Harmony per-tool
envelopes; a content-only turn on a tool-call message is a miss), WholeBody
renders such a message without its tool calls and replays the stored body
once in the content slot (one R..A span when the turn reasoned). Only the
Qwen4 render (render_qwen4_prompt_history, AR and native MTP) passes
WholeBody; dense Qwen, the VMM batch render and other families keep
Envelopes.

Identity: a tool-call turn is keyed by each call's name and canonical
arguments (asst_turn_fingerprint), so an edited call misses; under WholeBody
prose the client echoes with the calls must also equal the emitted prose
(empty content is accepted), so edited prose misses instead of replaying the
original. A miss falls back to the template render of that turn.

Session-exact like every live continuation: the cache-off prompt is the same
spliced render, only the reuse differs.

Tests: prompt_frame (WholeBody extends with and without reasoning, Envelopes
and a lookup miss equal the plain render, bytes the template would rewrite);
qwen_history_chain_tests::whole_body_tool_turn_replays_emitted_ids_and_edited_turns_miss
(edited arguments, name and prose each fall back to the template render with
none of the stale emitted ids). GPU-free oracle on the real Flash-Next
tokenizer and template: template_cache_eval --qwen-tool-turns <metadata.json>
(--features lab).

entry.desc: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next MQ3 XTS: 3-bit GPTQ (W3) on 16,839 of the 24,576 trunk routed experts; the other 7,737 experts and every other tensor are the MQ4 XTS bytes (Qwen4 HFQM, arch 16). Split base (59.3 GB) with no PLE rows of its own: it loads them from the shared qwen3.8-flash-next.ple-q4 (29.1 GB) or exact .ple-q8 (54.4 GB), bound by row geometry and the q8 source-rows SHA-256, so the download is about 88.4 GB with the q4 rows or 113.7 GB with the q8 rows. Needs hipfire at or after a6f241ce2 (split-base PLE loader).

sources.release_top_excerpt:
# Changelog

## v0.4.2.1 — 2026-10-14

- **Strix Halo NPU trunk: the built-in calibration now applies on any Halo kernel and NPU firmware.** `npu_trunk=auto` armed only when the compiled-in Halo calibration matched the host exactly, including the kernel release, NPU firmware and NPU PCI slot of the machine it was measured on, so every stock-kernel Halo logged `npu-trunk: off (calibration key mismatch: kernel.uname_release)` and served GPU-only. For the built-in calibration those three fields are now advisory: when any differs, it is used with its margin raised to 0.05 (the pipe must be predicted at least 5% faster than GPU-only, since the timings were measured on a different kernel/firmware), and the load logs `npu-trunk: built-in calibration measured on <kernel>/<fw>, this host <kernel>/<fw>; using it with margin 0.05`. Arch, build, model-index hash, epilogue and trunk route stay strict, and a user calibration file stays fully strict. Output is exact on either route; the calibration only chooses between them. First-load self-calibration is planned.
- **The NPU trunk calibration identity is pinned to `hipfire-0.4.2:npu-trunk-bf16-rowmajor-v1`.** It no longer derives from the crate version: it names the NPU serving numerics/transport, which a release bump does not change. Deriving it from the crate version would have orphaned the shipped Halo calibrations and left `npu_trunk=auto` GPU-only on 0.4.2.1.
- **Flash-Next: tool-call turns in the history replay the tokens the model emitted.** A follow-up turn whose history held an assistant tool call rendered that turn through the chat template. That stays a strict extension of the committed conversation only while the model's output is exactly the template's own canonical tokenization; a different BPE split of the emitted text, or spacing the template rewrites around `<tool_call>`, made the follow-up miss its live continuation and re-prefill the whole conversation. Qwen4 now replays a cached tool-call turn as the whole body the model emitted (reasoning, prose and every `<tool_call>` block), as it already did for plain turns, so the follow-up no longer depends on that. On Strix Halo with canonical model output both builds already continued in place: a 7-request tool chain and a 32K-context tool append reused every committed token before and after, with identical output. The cache key covers each call's name and arguments, and prose the client echoes with the calls must equal the emitted prose (empty content is accepted); an edited turn misses and falls back to the template render. Session-exact like every live continuation. Other model families keep the template render (`ToolTurnSplice::Envelopes`). `HIPFIRE_SESSION_CACHE_BYTES=0` turns reuse off.
- **Flash-Next session reuse is traceable per request.** With `HIPFIRE_QWEN_CACHE_TRACE=1`, every Qwen4 request (native MTP and AR) prints `[qwen4-session] route=… prompt=… prior=… lcp=… reused=… new=… source=live|snapshot|cold`: the previous turn's committed history, its common prefix with the new canonical prompt, and what the session cache reused. When the prompt diverges from that history, `[qwen4-session ids]` shows the token ids around the first difference. Host-side only; off by default.
- Changelog correction: the Flash-Next session cache's resident snapshot for deep appends past the pool budget (#847, HIPF-46, @fivetide; +512 tokens on a 256K prefix 4.7 → 197.5 tok/s on Strix Halo) shipped in v0.4.2 but was missing from its notes.
